findings.summary: The file list is a headerless <table> used as a single-select list: the selected file is only highlighted and bolded, so screen readers never hear which file is open.
findings.fix: Render a listbox: wrapper role="listbox" aria-label={t('app.fileList')} tabIndex={0} aria-activedescendant={'file-row-'+encodeURIComponent(selectedFile?.name)}, each row role="option" aria-selected={selectedFile?.name===f.name} tabIndex={-1}. Or use a <ul> of native <button aria-current={isSelected ? 'true' : undefined}>.

findings.summary: Moonstone TableRow adds tabIndex=0 to every file row, but rows only handle onClick: Tab lands on each file and Enter/Space do nothing. The list costs one tab stop per file plus one for the container.
findings.fix: When adopting the listbox pattern, pass tabIndex={-1} to every TableRow (props spread after Moonstone's tabIndex: 0) and let the container own focus. Activate on Enter/Space too: onKeyDown={e => (e.key==='Enter'||e.key===' ') && (e.preventDefault(), handleFileClick(f))}.
findings.evidence: Moonstone TableRow: createElement('tr', {..., tabIndex: 0, ...props}); module passes only onClick

findings.summary: The scroll container is focusable (tabIndex=0) and changes the selection with Arrow keys, but it has no role or accessible name: screen readers announce an unnamed group with no hint that arrows select a file.
findings.fix: Give it the listbox role and a name (role="listbox" aria-label={t('app.fileList')}) and aria-activedescendant on the selected option, or remove tabIndex if the rows themselves become buttons.

findings.summary: Whether a file is enabled or disabled is shown only by a 3px green/grey bar and a strikethrough, neither of which reaches the accessibility tree, so screen reader users cannot tell disabled configurations apart.
findings.fix: Add text: inside the status cell render {f.enabled ? t('app.status.enabled') : t('app.status.disabled')}, or append it to the option's accessible name (aria-label={`${f.name}, ${statusLabel}, ${badgeLabel}`}). Mark the bar aria-hidden="true".

findings.summary: The compact ConfigStateBadge renders an icon-only Chip with label '' (Module / Module default / User) whose meaning exists only in a hover tooltip on a non-focusable div, so keyboard and screen reader users never get the state.
findings.fix: In ConfigStateBadge compact mode, keep the text for AT (aria-label alone is not reliable on a role-less div): render {t(config.labelKey)} beside the icon (or role="img" aria-label={t(config.labelKey)} on the Chip).
findings.evidence: const label = compact ? '' : t(config.labelKey); <Chip icon={<config.icon/>} label={label} />

findings.summary: The 'Search in content' Switch renders <input type=checkbox> with no accessible name: the visible Typography beside it is not associated, and the Tooltip describes the wrapping div, not the input.
findings.fix: Associate the visible text: <Switch id="deep-search-switch" ... /> and <Typography component="label" htmlFor="deep-search-switch">{t('app.searchDeep')}</Typography> (Switch spreads rest props onto the input). Alternatively aria-label={t('app.searchDeep')} plus aria-describedby to the tooltip text.

findings.summary: Moonstone SearchInput inputs (file filter and .cfg property filter) are named only by their placeholder and sit in an unlabelled role="search" landmark Moonstone adds, so the field's name disappears once text is typed.
findings.fix: Pass a name to the input (SearchInput forwards rest props to <input>): aria-label={t('app.searchLabel')} in FileSidebar.jsx:101 and aria-label={t('editor.filter.label')} in CfgEditor.jsx:528. Add the keys to every locale file.

findings.summary: The Visual/Raw mode selector is a Moonstone Dropdown whose trigger is a div role="listbox" named by the current value ('Visual Edit'), with no aria-expanded or popup semantics: users hear a listbox, not an editor-mode control.
findings.fix: Use a two-state control: <div role="group" aria-label={t('editor.mode.label')}> with two Moonstone Buttons, each aria-pressed={isRawMode === (value==='raw')}, disabled={isLoadingFile}. Or a RadioGroup. If Dropdown stays, at least wrap it in role="group" aria-label={t('editor.mode.label')}.
findings.evidence: <Dropdown data-cy="editor-mode-dropdown" value={isRawMode ? 'raw' : 'visual'} data={modeOptions} .../> -> <div role="listbox" aria-label="Visual Edit" tabIndex=0>

findings.summary: role="toolbar" is set on the header actions without an accessible name or the toolbar keyboard model (one tab stop, arrow keys), so it promises behaviour that is not there.
findings.fix: Either drop role="toolbar" (three independent buttons need no composite role), or keep it with aria-label={t('app.actions')} and a roving tabindex handling ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End.

findings.summary:
The selected file name is styled as a heading (Typography variant 'heading') but renders a

, so after the page

there is no heading for the open configuration to navigate to.
findings.fix: Pass a heading element: typographyProps={{variant: 'heading', component: 'h2'}}. Do the same for the dialog titles in DiffModal.tsx:131 and CfgMetatypePropertyDialog.jsx:109 and reference them with aria-labelledby.

findings.summary: When the raw/YAML content is invalid, Save is silently disabled; the Monaco markers are not announced and nothing tells a screen reader user why Save is unavailable.
findings.fix:
Render a status message when !isYamlValid, e.g.

{t('editor.invalidContent')}

, and link it: aria-describedby={isSaveDisabled && !isYamlValid ? 'save-blocked-reason' : undefined} on the Save button. Moonstone Button spreads rest props onto

findings.summary: Toasts (save succeeded, errors, warnings) are mounted on demand in a plain Moonstone Paper <section> with no live region, so screen readers never announce the outcome of save, delete, upload or encryption actions.
findings.fix:
Keep a live region always mounted and change only its text:
{toast?.type !== 'error' ? toast?.message : ''}
plus a role="alert" region for errors; keep the visual Paper aria-hidden="true" or put the role on it while it stays mounted.

findings.summary: StatusBanner shows load errors and the Module / Module-default warnings when a file opens, but has no role, so screen readers are not told that the file failed to load or is managed by a module.
findings.fix: Map tone to a role: <div role={tone === 'error' ? 'alert' : 'status'} ...>. Because banners mount with the file, render the role container once in index.jsx and swap its text, or accept that role=alert on mount is announced. Mark the tone icon aria-hidden="true".
findings.evidence:
export const StatusBanner = ({tone = 'info', message, dataCy}) => ...
{icon}{message}

findings.summary: InlineLoader ('Loading files…', 'Loading file…') is a CSS spinner with text and no status role; the loading state and its end are not announced and the editor pane carries no aria-busy.
findings.fix:
…spinner aria-hidden="true"…{label}
, and aria-busy={loadingFile} on the editor container in index.jsx:281.

findings.summary: The 'Matching properties: N' count appears and changes while filtering but is not a live region, so screen reader users typing in the filter get no feedback about results.
findings.fix: Keep the element mounted and live: <Typography role="status" aria-live="polite" data-cy="cfg-filter-count">{filtering ? t('editor.filter.count', {count}) : ''}</Typography>.

findings.summary: In the create dialog, metatype and factory choices are clickable <div>s with no role, tabindex or key handler, and selection is shown by background only: keyboard and screen reader users cannot create from a template or factory.
findings.fix: Make the list a single-select group: container role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby the 'Template'/'Factory' heading; each card role="radio" aria-checked={isSelected} tabIndex={isSelected||first ? 0 : -1} with Arrow-key roving and Space/Enter to select. Native <input type="radio"> in a <label> is simpler and preferred.

findings.summary:
Dialog inputs (manual file name, filter, factory identifier, prompt) are named only by placeholders; their bold Typography 'labels' render

and are not associated, so the name disappears once text is entered.
findings.fix: Associate the visible text: give each Typography component="label" htmlFor and the Input a matching id (Moonstone Input forwards id), e.g. <Typography component="label" htmlFor="create-manual">…</Typography><Input id="create-manual" …/>. For the prompt (line 301) use aria-labelledby the ModalHeader message.

findings.summary: When the factory identifier already exists, a red caption appears and Create is disabled, but the input is not marked invalid nor linked to the message, so screen reader users do not learn why.
findings.fix: <Input id="factory-id" aria-invalid={isFactoryIdentifierTaken} aria-describedby={isFactoryIdentifierTaken ? 'factory-id-error' : 'factory-id-hint'} …/> and <Typography id="factory-id-error" role="alert" …>. Give the suggested-filename caption id="factory-id-hint".

findings.summary: The create-dialog tabs come from Moonstone (role=tablist/tab, aria-selected) but the tablist is unnamed, tabs have no aria-controls, and the content below is not a role="tabpanel"; Moonstone also leaves every tab at tabIndex 0.
findings.fix: <Tab aria-label={t('modal.create.tabs.label')}>; <TabItem id={`create-tab-${tab.id}`} aria-controls="create-tabpanel" tabIndex={activeCreateTab===tab.id ? 0 : -1} …/>; wrap the active content in <div id="create-tabpanel" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby={`create-tab-${activeCreateTab}`}>. TabItem spreads rest props after its own.

findings.summary: Moonstone Modal sets aria-labelledby to its own id, so the dialog's accessible name is computed from all of its content (title, message, inputs, buttons) instead of the title.
findings.fix: Override from the module (Modal spreads rest props last): and {config.title}}>{showModalMessage ? {config.message} : null}.

findings.summary: The icon-only close button of ModalDialog is labelled 'Cancel', the same name as the footer Cancel button, so two controls share one name while the icon reads as 'close'.
findings.fix: aria-label={t('modal.close')} (add the key to every locale) and keep the footer button as Cancel.

findings.summary: In the review-before-save diff, added and removed lines are distinguished only by green/red colour on plain <span>s, so screen reader users (and users who cannot see colour) cannot tell what will change.
findings.fix: Render semantic changes with a text cue: part.added ? : part.removed ? : , and prefix each with {t('modal.diff.added')} / removed (or a visible +/− gutter). Note many screen readers ignore / by default, so keep the text prefix.

findings.summary: The diff dialog's close control is a <div onClick> wrapping the Close icon: not focusable, no role, no name, so it is invisible to keyboard and screen reader users (Escape and Cancel still work).
findings.fix: <Button variant="ghost" icon={<Close/>} aria-label={t('modal.close')} onClick={onClose}/> (Moonstone renders a native <button>). Drop the inline hover colour handlers.

findings.summary:
The dialog name is a copy of the visible title passed as aria-label instead of a reference to it, and the title itself renders as a

; the two can drift apart and the title is not a heading.
findings.fix: Render the title as a heading with an id and reference it: <Typography id="diff-modal-title" component="h2" …> and aria-labelledby="diff-modal-title" on the role="dialog" element.
findings.evidence: role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label={t('modal.diff.title', { name: filename })} ... <Typography variant="heading" weight="bold">

findings.summary: The property-picker dialog's close control is a <div onClick> around the Close icon: not focusable, no role, no accessible name.
findings.fix: <Button variant="ghost" icon={<Close/>} aria-label={t('modal.close')} onClick={onClose}/>.

findings.summary: The property search field is named only by its placeholder, the result count is never announced, and the 'already exists' message is not linked to the field.
findings.fix: <Input aria-label={t('editor.metatype.cfgPicker.searchLabel')} aria-describedby="cfg-picker-feedback" aria-invalid={customAlreadyExists} …/>, give the feedback block id="cfg-picker-feedback" role="status", and add a polite count ("{n} properties") there.

findings.summary: aria-label={property.id} on each option button replaces its visible content, so the type, default value and description shown to sighted users are dropped from what screen readers hear.
findings.fix: Remove the aria-label so the name comes from the content, or keep it and add aria-describedby pointing at an id on the details block (type, default, description).

findings.summary: The visual editor's header row uses TableBodyCell (<td>) inside <thead>, and three header cells are empty, so cells are not associated with 'Property', 'Value', 'Security' columns.
findings.fix: Render header cells as <th scope="col">: <TableBodyCell component="th" scope="col" …> (TableBodyCell accepts component) or Moonstone TableHeadCell, and give the empty ones visually hidden text (Reorder, Type, Actions). Same fix in Editor.jsx:326.

findings.summary: Every key, value and comment field in the visual editor is an unlabelled <textarea>/<input> (placeholder 'Key'/'Value' at best), so a screen reader hears 'edit text' with no clue which property a value belongs to.
findings.fix: Name each field from its row: key aria-label={t('editor.aria.key', {line: index + 1})}; value aria-label={t('editor.aria.value', {key: key || index + 1})} on AutoResizeTextArea (line 750) and the masked Input (line 735); comment aria-label={t('editor.aria.comment', {line: index + 1})} (line 652).

findings.summary: The per-row 'encrypt' Checkbox has no accessible name (the title sits on the <td>, not the input), so users hear 'checkbox, not checked' without knowing it encrypts that property's value.
findings.fix: <Checkbox aria-label={t('editor.aria.encrypt', {key})} …/> (Moonstone Checkbox forwards rest props to the <input>). Same defect in Editor.jsx:125.

findings.summary: Row delete buttons are icon-only and named solely by a title ('Delete this property'), identical on every row; title-only names are unreliable and do not say which property is deleted.
findings.fix: aria-label={t('editor.aria.deleteProperty', {key: key || t('editor.emptyLine')})} on the Button (rest props reach <button>); keep title or a Tooltip for sighted users. Apply the same to the show/hide-secret button (line 764) and Editor.jsx:131.
findings.evidence: <Button data-cy={`cfg-delete-${index}`} icon={<Close />} variant="ghost" color="danger" size="small" title={t('tooltip.deleteProperty')} />

findings.summary: Keyboard reordering moves the entry but rows are keyed by index, so focus stays on the handle of whichever entry now occupies that slot; the move is not announced and every handle has the same name.
findings.fix: After handleReorder(index, index±1), focus the handle at the new index (ref map + requestAnimationFrame), announce via a polite live region ('{key} moved to position {n} of {total}'), and name each handle with its key: aria-label={t('editor.reorderHandleFor', {key})}. Key rows by a stable id instead of index.
findings.evidence: <TableRow key={index} ...> ... onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === 'ArrowUp' && index > 0) { e.preventDefault(); handleReorder(index, index - 1); } ...

findings.summary: The Metatype info marker is a div showing the letter 'i' whose documentation lives in a hover-only Tooltip; it is not focusable, so keyboard users cannot read the property documentation and screen readers just read 'i'.
findings.fix: Use a button: <button type="button" aria-label={t('editor.metatype.aboutProperty', {key})} aria-describedby={`cfg-doc-${index}`}>i</button> and render the documentation in an element with that id (visually hidden or a toggletip opened on click/Enter, dismissible with Escape).

findings.summary: 'Toggle Comments' and 'Toggle Empty Lines' are toggle buttons whose on/off state is shown only by an eye icon; no aria-pressed, so screen readers cannot tell whether comments are shown.
findings.fix: Pass aria-pressed={showComments} and aria-pressed={showEmptyLines} to the Buttons (Moonstone Button spreads rest props onto <button>). Avoid Moonstone ButtonToggle here: it calls blur() on click, dropping keyboard focus.

findings.summary: The selected row, which decides where 'Add property/comment/empty line' inserts, is shown only by a background colour, so screen reader users cannot tell where new entries will go.
findings.fix: Expose the current row: aria-current="true" on the selected TableRow (or aria-selected inside a grid), and include the insertion point in the add buttons' description, e.g. aria-describedby to 'Inserted after line {n}'.

findings.summary: monaco.editor.create is called without ariaLabel, so the raw editor is announced with Monaco's generic name and nothing says which file or format is being edited.
findings.fix: Add ariaLabel: t('editor.raw.ariaLabel', {name: filename}) and keep Monaco's hint in it (e.g. '… Press Alt+F1 for accessibility options'), since overriding ariaLabel removes Monaco's default hint. Update it with editor.updateOptions when filename changes.
findings.evidence: monaco.editor.create(containerRef.current, { value, language, theme, minimap: { enabled: false }, lineNumbers: 'on', ... })  // no ariaLabel

findings.summary: Secrets are masked only by a CSS inline decoration (transparent text); the characters stay in the model, so Monaco's screen-reader textarea and hover/announce paths read the secret aloud while sighted users see dots.
findings.fix: Treat AT like the visual editor: when secrets are masked and accessibilitySupport is on, either make the editor readOnly with a masked copy, or hand Monaco a masked model and map edits back. At minimum document it and default secretsVisible=false to a read-only view for AT.

findings.summary: 'Add property' opens the Metatype side panel but does not expose aria-expanded/aria-controls, and the panel is an unlabelled div that does not receive focus, so screen reader users are not told it appeared.
findings.fix: On the button: aria-expanded={showPropertyPanel} aria-controls="metatype-property-panel". On the panel: id="metatype-property-panel" role="region" aria-labelledby its heading (render the 'Available properties' Typography as an h3 with an id), and move focus to the search input when it opens; return focus to the button on Hide.
findings.evidence: <RawToolbarButton dataCy="editor-add-metatype-property" onClick={() => supportsMetatypeAssistance && setShowPropertyPanel(true)} ... /> ... <div data-cy="metatype-property-panel" style={RAW_EDITOR_PANEL_STYLE}>

findings.summary: The Metatype property search field in the raw editor's side panel has no accessible name beyond its placeholder.
findings.fix: aria-label={t('editor.metatype.searchLabel')} on the Input (forwarded to <input>), or a visible <label htmlFor>.

findings.summary: Every property card has an 'Insert' (or 'Already present') button with the same name, so in a buttons list screen reader users cannot tell which property each one inserts.
findings.fix: aria-label={t('editor.metatype.insertNamed', {name: property.id})} (and the 'already present' variant), keeping the visible 'Insert' text at the start of the name (2.5.3).

findings.summary: The full-text previews for truncated names and values appear on mouse hover only, with pointer-events: none (cannot be hovered) and no Escape dismissal; keyboard users never see them.
findings.fix: Also show the preview on focus of the focusable ancestor, drop pointerEvents:'none' or keep it open while hovered, close on Escape, and mark it role="tooltip" referenced by aria-describedby. Same pattern in CfgEditor.jsx:507 and Editor.jsx:291.

findings.summary: The tree editor's group rows expand and collapse through onClick on a <td>, with no button, no aria-expanded and no keyboard handler, so nested groups cannot be opened from the keyboard.
findings.fix: Put a native toggle in the cell: <button type="button" aria-expanded={!isCollapsed} onClick={toggleCollapse}>{chevron aria-hidden}{displayLabel}</button>, or adopt role="treegrid" with aria-level/aria-expanded on rows.

findings.summary: Leaf values in the tree editor become editable only on double-click of a plain div, which has no role, tabindex or key handler; keyboard users cannot edit values there.
findings.fix: Render a <button type="button" aria-label={t('editor.aria.editValue', {key: rowLabel})} onClick={…setEditingValueKey(keyString)}> or an always-present labelled input; name the edit Input/textarea (lines 87-99) and the encrypt Checkbox (line 125).

passed: No role="button"/"link"/"checkbox" or landmark roles added to native elements in module code (no redundant ARIA authored by the module).
No positive tabindex values in module code.
No aria-labelledby / aria-describedby / aria-controls IDREFs authored by the module, hence none broken (dangling references come from Moonstone, see notes).
Custom dialogs DiffModal and CfgMetatypePropertyDialog use role="dialog" + aria-modal="true" and useDialogA11y: focus moves in, Tab/Shift+Tab trapped, Escape closes, focus restored to the trigger.
Moonstone Modal (ModalDialog) uses floating-ui FloatingFocusManager with role=dialog and aria-modal.
CfgEditor reorder handle is a native <button> with an aria-label and an Arrow Up/Down alternative to drag-and-drop (2.5.7).
Show/hide secret buttons (CfgEditor.jsx:764) carry an aria-label that switches with state.
Metatype property options in CfgMetatypePropertyDialog are native <button type="button"> elements.
Header, file toolbar, raw-editor toolbar and footer buttons all have visible text labels; no icon-only button there lacks a name.
Hidden file input (display:none) is only triggered from the labelled Import button.
Page title is a real <h1> (AppHeaderBar Typography component="h1").
notes: Moonstone defects the module can only work around: Dropdown puts role="listbox" on the trigger with a role="option" span and no aria-expanded; Modal labels itself (aria-labelledby = its own id); TableRow forces tabIndex=0; TabItem keeps every tab at tabIndex 0 (no roving) and arrows do not wrap; Switch and Checkbox add redundant role="checkbox"/aria-checked on native checkboxes; Tooltip clones aria-describedby="moonstone-tooltip_label" (a constant id, absent from the DOM while closed, duplicated if two tooltips open); SearchInput wraps the field in an unlabelled role="search" landmark; clear buttons use a hardcoded English aria-label "Reset"; ModalHeader renders an <h4> (level skip from the page h1); icons are <svg> without aria-hidden. Worth an upstream Moonstone issue.

Tooltips that repeat the button label (Cancel: tooltip 'Cancel'; Save: 'Save changes' vs 'Save Changes') add a redundant aria-describedby; tooltips on disabled buttons (Mark as Default, Save) are unreachable by keyboard because disabled buttons cannot take focus.

AppHeaderBar renders <header>; outside a sectioning element it maps to a banner landmark. Whether that duplicates the Jahia admin shell's banner, and whether a <main> wraps the route, must be checked in the runtime scan.

Editor.jsx (ConfigEditor tree) is only reached for files whose extension is not lowercase .cfg/.yml (index.jsx tests endsWith case-sensitively while the server lowercases), so its findings are low confidence for reachability, not for the defects.

Behavioural bug seen while reviewing: the keyboard reorder handler (CfgEditor.jsx:614) does not check `filtering`, unlike the drag path, so Arrow Up/Down reorders against hidden neighbours while a filter is active.
Monaco captures Tab inside the editor; the escape (Ctrl+M / tab focus mode) is only discoverable through Alt+F1. Keep that hint in any custom ariaLabel (2.1.2).
Selection-follows-focus in the file list: Arrow Up/Down opens each file (and the unsaved-changes dialog when dirty). With a listbox, consider moving focus with arrows and opening on Enter.
Not checked here (runtime half): computed accessible names in the browser, Moonstone Menu roles when the Dropdown is open, focus order across panes, contrast of state colours.
